stories.text: Just weeks after winning his second World Series championship, Pittsburgh Pirates manager Danny Murtaugh announces his retirement. The 53-year-old Murtaugh has a history of health issues and was briefly hospitalized during 1971 for chest pain; his decision ends the third of four terms he will serve as the team's manager. The Pirates name coach and former centerfielder Bill Virdon as Murtaugh's successor.
stories.headline: Just Weeks After Winning His Second World Series Championship
stories.extract: Daniel Edward Murtaugh was an American second baseman, manager, front-office executive, and coach in Major League Baseball (MLB). Gallegos made his MLB debut in 2017 with the Yankees and also pitched for them in 2018 before being traded to the Cardinals.

stories.text: The Los Angeles Dodgers hired Dave Roberts as their new manager. Roberts will succeed Don Mattingly, who mutually parted ways with the Dodgers last month after five years with the team. Roberts, whose father is an African-American former Marine and mother is a Japanese-American, becomes the first minority manager of the storied franchise that signed the first African-American player, Jackie Robinson.

stories.text: After 20 seasons and 356 victories, most-ever by an MLB left-hander, Warren Spahn and the Braves sever their relationship when Milwaukee sells the future Hall of Famer's contract to the New York Mets. Spahn, 43, had posted his poorest season in 1964—going 6–13 (5.29) in 38 games. Determined to prolong his playing career, he had turned down the Braves' offer of three off-field jobs in their organization.
